definition: Galaxy AI is a collection of artificial intelligence (AI) features developed by Samsung Electronics for use in Galaxy-branded mobile devices.
details: First released with the Samsung Galaxy S24 series in January 2024, the system integrates both on-device and cloud-based processing to support features such as language translation, image editing, and content search. These tools operate within various Samsung applications and are intended to assist with everyday tasks. According to Samsung: "In essence, Bixby is like a personal assistant ready to respond to your verbal commands, while Galaxy AI is like a smart companion that's always working to make your device smarter and your life easier."

explainer.lead: Galaxy AI is Samsung’s umbrella for AI helpers built into Galaxy mobile devices and their apps. It handles tasks such as translating language, editing images, and finding content, using processing on the phone, in the cloud, or both.

tiers.eli5: Galaxy AI is like a set of helpful tools tucked into a Samsung Galaxy phone. One tool can help translate words, another can help change a picture, and another can help you find things. Some work happens on the phone itself, while some uses computers elsewhere through the cloud.
tiers.practitioner: Treat Galaxy AI as an application-level feature set rather than a standalone model or developer library. It runs within Samsung applications on Galaxy-branded mobile devices, beginning with the Galaxy S24 series in January 2024, and combines on-device and cloud-based processing. Do not assume that every feature executes locally or that Galaxy AI and Bixby are interchangeable.
tiers.paperLevel: Galaxy AI can be described as a device-integrated feature set F, where each feature maps user input in a Samsung application to an AI-assisted output using execution e in {on-device, cloud-based}. It was first released with the Samsung Galaxy S24 series in January 2024. It is a product-level system description, not a specification of one model architecture, training method, or evaluation metric.

explainer.example: A Galaxy S24 user chooses an image-editing feature while working with a photo in a Samsung app. Galaxy AI processes the editing request on the device, through the cloud, or using both, then provides the edited image for the user to continue working with.

explainer.intuition: Instead of being one app you open, Galaxy AI is a layer of assistance spread across familiar Samsung apps. It brings several AI capabilities together so common phone tasks can be completed where they already happen.
howItWorks: A user starts a supported task, such as translating text or editing an image, in a Samsung application.
The app passes the relevant content to the appropriate Galaxy AI feature.
Processing takes place on the device, through cloud-based processing, or through a combination of both.
The resulting translation, edit, or search result is returned for use within the device’s apps.
explainer.whyItMatters: Galaxy AI puts several kinds of AI assistance directly into everyday mobile workflows rather than treating them as separate destinations. Its hybrid processing design also means the system is not limited to doing all of its work on the phone.
misconceptions: Galaxy AI is a collection of features, not a single app or a single named AI model.
It is not entirely on-device: Samsung describes both on-device and cloud-based processing.
It is not the same as Bixby; Samsung compares Bixby to a personal assistant responding to verbal commands and Galaxy AI to a companion making the device smarter.
